put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

affiliation_kind.description: What kind of affiliation the item is.

organisation_identifier.description: The organisation's identifier, where ORCID gives one: a URL for ROR, else as given.

organisation_identifier_scheme.description: The scheme of organisation_identifier, in ORCID's words, such as ROR, GRID or RINGGOLD. Present exactly when organisation_identifier is.

end_year.description: The year it ended; absent while it continues.

Affiliation.title: Affiliation

AffiliationKind.description: The kinds of affiliation an ORCID record holds.
AffiliationKind.title: AffiliationKind

ChosenRepository.description: The repository a researcher chose to deposit the project's data in, from the shortlist, by its re3data identifier: the conductor fills it into a Message, and into the input of an agent that mixes in GivenProjectRepository, so that the agent knows a repository is chosen and which (docs/specs/projects.md). The last choice stands until a researcher chooses again.

chosen_repository_name.description: The chosen repository's name, as the pinned re3data export gives it.

chosen_re3data_id.description: The chosen repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100010468.

ChosenRepository.title: ChosenRepository

ConversationTurn.description: One earlier turn of a conversation, as the caller presents it to the agent. An agent turn names the agent and version that produced it and the invocation it came from.

turn_text.description: What was said in the turn.

turn_agent_id.description: For an agent turn, the agent that produced it.

turn_agent_version.description: For an agent turn, the version of the agent that produced it.

turn_invocation_id.description: For an agent turn, the invocation it came from.

ConversationTurn.title: ConversationTurn

DocumentKind.description: What a project document is for (docs/specs/projects.md).
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

DocumentationSummary.description: What one document a researcher attached to a project is, without its text: the conductor fills one per document into a Message so that the agent knows the project holds it (docs/specs/projects.md).

documentation_name.description: The file name the researcher attached the document under, without any folder.

documentation_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the document's UTF-8 text, by which the project keeps it.

documentation_media_type.description: The document's media type, text/plain or text/markdown.

documentation_size.description: The size of the document's UTF-8 text, in bytes.

documentation_added_at.description: When the document was added to the project.

documentation_source_media_type.description: The media type of the Word document or PDF the document's text was read from, inside the deployment; absent for a document attached as text. The project keeps the file beside the text.

DocumentationSummary.title: DocumentationSummary

DraftSummary.description: The latest version of one document drafted in a project, without its text: the conductor fills one per document into a Message so that the agent knows which version is current and whether it was drafted from the inventory the project holds now, rather than relying on what it said of an earlier version (docs/specs/projects.md).

version.description: The number of a version within its document, counted from 1.

version_state.description: Whether a person has approved or rejected the version, or not yet decided.

drafted_since_inventory.description: Whether the version was drafted after the project's inventory was last added or revised, so that it reflects which files the inventory now lists. Absent when the project holds no inventory.

DraftSummary.title: DraftSummary

ExternalIdentifier.description: An identifier from another scheme, as an ORCID record gives it: for a researcher, such as a Scopus Author ID; for a work, such as a DOI.

identifier_type.description: The scheme, in ORCID's words, such as doi or Scopus Author ID.

identifier_url.description: The identifier as a URL, where the record gives one.

ExternalIdentifier.title: ExternalIdentifier

FactKind.description: What a project fact is about (docs/specs/projects.md).
FactKind.title: FactKind

FileDecision.description: Whether a file of the inventory is to be deposited.
FileDecision.title: FileDecision

IntakeAnswer.description: The researcher's current answer to one of the intake's setup questions beside the entry question (dd_sdk.intake), as the project log shows it, with the labels of the options chosen (docs/specs/orchestration.md, invariant 20).

intake_question_prompt.description: The intake question as the researcher was asked it.

intake_answer_labels.description: The labels of the options the researcher chose, such as "Not sure"; never empty.

IntakeAnswer.title: IntakeAnswer

InventoryFormat.description: The files of one media type in a project's inventory, without their paths: the conductor fills one per media type into an InventorySummary, so that the agent knows what kinds of files the dataset holds without asking (docs/specs/projects.md, #1287).

format_media_type.description: The media type (MIME type) of the group's files. Absent, the group is of the files whose media type could not be told.

format_pronom_ids.description: Every PRONOM unique identifier (PUID) the group's files matched, sorted.

format_file_count.description: How many of the inventory's files are in the group.

InventoryFormat.title: InventoryFormat

InventorySummary.description: What the inventory a project holds is, without its files: the conductor fills it into a Message so that the agent knows the project has one (docs/specs/projects.md).

inventory_digest.description: The inventory's dd-input-json-v1 hash, by which the project keeps it.

inventory_file_count.description: How many files the inventory lists.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

inventory_added_at.description: When the inventory was added to the project, as its latest; a revision, such as files left out in Edit inventory, is added anew.

inventory_revised_from_file_count.description: How many files the inventory it replaced listed. Absent when it is the first the project holds.

inventory_formats.description: The inventory's files grouped by media type, the group with the most bytes first, as the app's inventory view groups them. Absent, the summary was made without them.

inventory_table_count.description: How many of the inventory's files are tables whose fields it lists.

InventorySummary.title: InventorySummary

LocationPrecision.description: The precision at which a location may be published.
LocationPrecision.title: LocationPrecision

ProjectFact.description: One fact about a project that a check agent proposes and a person confirms: a funder, a repository a funder or institution requires, whether a file is deposited, whether a sensitive field or file may be published and at what precision, the licence, or an output a data management plan committed to share (docs/specs/projects.md). fact_kind says which of the value slots apply; fact_subject is the key a person's decision counts by, so the last decision on a subject stands. An agent's payload carries proposals in proposed_facts; only a person's decision makes one a fact, and the conductor gives the facts a person decided to every drafter and orchestrator in the project as project_decisions, without proposed_because.

fact_kind.description: What the fact is about, which says which value slots apply.

fact_subject.description: The key a decision counts by within its kind: the funder's identifier or name, the repository's re3data identifier or name, the file's path, the field or path judged sensitive, or licence. The last decision on a kind and subject stands.

fact_funder_name.description: The funder's name, as its policy record or the researcher gives it.

fact_funder_ror.description: The funder's ROR identifier, as a URL, where it is known.

fact_crossref_funder_id.description: The funder's Crossref Funder ID, as a DOI URL, where it is known.

fact_re3data_id.description: The required repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100010199, where known.

fact_required_by.description: The funders, journals or institutions that require the repository.

fact_file_path.description: The path of the file the fact is about, relative to the dataset's root folder, as the inventory gives it.

file_decision.description: Whether the file is to be deposited.

fact_check_kind.description: The kind of check that raised the fact, in the checking agent's words, such as duplicate, system_file or third_party. Kept as it was given; the core does not enumerate it.

sensitive_subject.description: The field name, or the file path, judged sensitive, such as a lat or lon field, or a file of site coordinates.

sensitivity_decision.description: Whether the sensitive field or file may be published, and how.

location_precision.description: For a location that may be published or generalised, the precision agreed. Absent where the subject is not a location.

licence_id.description: The licence decided, as an SPDX identifier or a URL.

commitment_repository.description: For a sharing commitment, the repository the plan committed to share the output in, as the plan names it; absent where it names none. A plan that names several for one output gives a sharing commitment for each.

commitment_access.description: For a sharing commitment, how openly the plan committed to share the output (such as open, embargoed or on request), as the plan says it; absent where it says nothing.

commitment_licence.description: For a sharing commitment, the licence the plan committed to, as the plan names it; absent where it names none.

commitment_quote.description: For a sharing commitment, the plan's own words the commitment was read from, verbatim, so the person deciding can see the passage it rests on.

commitment_document.description: For a sharing commitment, the digest of the attached document's text (its documentation_digest) the quote is from.

proposed_because.description: Why the agent proposes the fact, in a sentence for the person deciding. Kept with the proposal and shown to the person, never given to an agent.

ProjectFact.title: ProjectFact

QuestionAnswer.description: The researcher's answer to one question of a reply, named by its question_key: the values of the options chosen, for a choice question, and the answer in their own words, for a text question or where a choice question allows it.

answered_key.description: The question_key of the question answered.

answer_values.description: The values of the options chosen, for a choice question; empty when the researcher answered in their own words, and always empty for a text question.

answer_words.description: The researcher's answer in their own words: the whole answer to a text question, or an answer given in place of an option where a choice question allows it.

QuestionAnswer.title: QuestionAnswer

ReplyAnswers.description: The researcher's answers to the questions the turn before asked, given together: one QuestionAnswer for each question answered, none for a question skipped. The app checks them against those questions before it sends the turn (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

answer_to.description: The invocation whose reply asked the questions.

given_answers.description: One answer for each question answered, in the order asked; at least one.

ReplyAnswers.title: ReplyAnswers

ResearcherFunding.description: One grant or award on an ORCID record, with its funder.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

funding_type.description: The kind of funding, in ORCID's words, such as grant or award.

funder_identifier.description: The funder's identifier, where ORCID gives one, such as a Crossref Funder ID.

funder_identifier_scheme.description: The scheme of funder_identifier, in ORCID's words, such as FUNDREF or ROR. Present exactly when funder_identifier is.

award_identifier.description: The grant number or award identifier, where the record gives one.

end_year.description: The year it ended; absent while it continues.

ResearcherFunding.title: ResearcherFunding

ResearcherLink.description: A web page the researcher lists on their ORCID record, such as a personal page.

link_title.description: The name the researcher gave the page.

ResearcherLink.title: ResearcherLink

ResearcherRecord.description: What one researcher in a project chose to keep from their public ORCID record: only the sections and items they ticked, in ORCID's own words, never edited by a person or a model. The conductor fills the project's records into a Message and a DraftRequest so that an agent can draft creators, affiliations, subjects and funding from them (docs/specs/projects.md). Email addresses are never kept, even public ones.

orcid_id.description: The researcher's ORCID iD, as its URL, such as https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097.

researcher_name.description: The researcher's name as their ORCID record gives it: the credit name, else the given and family names. Absent when they keep their name private or did not keep it.

other_names.description: Other names the researcher is known by, as their ORCID record lists them.

biography.description: The researcher's biography, as their ORCID record gives it.

keywords.description: The researcher's own keywords for their research, as their ORCID record lists them.

country.description: A country the researcher's ORCID record names, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

researcher_links.description: The web pages the researcher's ORCID record lists.

external_identifiers.description: The researcher's identifiers in other schemes, as their ORCID record lists them.

affiliations.description: The researcher's affiliations they kept, the current ones first.

works.description: The researcher's works they kept, the most recent first: at most 50 are offered, so that an agent's input stays bounded.

works_omitted.description: How many works the record held beyond the 50 offered. Absent when none were left out.

fundings.description: The researcher's grants and awards they kept, the current ones first.

record_retrieved_at.description: When the record was read from ORCID's public API.

record_source.description: The public API address the record was read from.

ResearcherRecord.title: ResearcherRecord

ResearcherWork.description: One work on an ORCID record, such as a journal article or a dataset.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

work_type.description: The work's type, in ORCID's words, such as journal-article or data-set.

publication_year.description: The year the work was published.

journal_title.description: Where the work was published, such as a journal's name.

work_identifiers.description: The work's identifiers, such as its DOI.

ResearcherWork.title: ResearcherWork

SensitivityDecision.description: Whether a sensitive field or file may be published.
SensitivityDecision.title: SensitivityDecision

StepProgress.description: How far one step of the Blueprint's process flow has gone, as the project log shows it: started, done or skipped. A step the list leaves out is open (docs/specs/orchestration.md).
StepProgress.title: StepProgress

StepState.description: How far a process-flow step has gone; a step with none of these states is open.
StepState.title: StepState

TurnRole.description: Who spoke in a conversation turn.
TurnRole.title: TurnRole

VersionState.description: The state of one version of a project document (ADR-0035 decision 6). Every version begins proposed; once approved or rejected, it does not change.
VersionState.title: VersionState

description: One conversational turn addressed to an agent: the text of the turn and the conversation so far. The history is part of the input, so the input hash covers everything the agent saw. In a project that holds an inventory, the conductor adds what it is (docs/specs/projects.md); in any project, it adds the entry point chosen, the progress the project log shows and the project's title, if it has one (docs/specs/orchestration.md). It adds the researcher facts people in the project chose to keep from their public ORCID records, the facts they decided, the repository they chose and the latest version of each document drafted in it (docs/specs/projects.md).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

message_text.description: What the user said in this turn.

history.description: The earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first.

project_inventory.description: The inventory the conversation's project holds, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds no inventory.

reply_answers.description: The researcher's answers to the questions the previous turn asked, when they answered them in the form. message_text still carries the answers as prose.

project_entry.description: The Blueprint entry point (1, 2 or 3) the researcher chose for the conversation's project, the latest chosen. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or none was chosen.

project_progress.description: The process-flow steps the conversation's project log shows started, done or skipped, in flow order. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project. Derived from the log on every turn, never stored.

project_title.description: The conversation's project's latest title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or the project has no title yet.

project_title_by_researcher.description: Whether a person gave the project its title, so that a model's would be refused; false while the project has no title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project.

project_documentation.description: The documents the conversation's project holds, without their text, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds none.

project_entry_by_researcher.description: Whether the researcher chose the project's entry point, so that a model's would be refused; false when an orchestrator's model recorded it. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or no entry point was recorded.

project_researchers.description: The researcher facts the conversation's project holds, one record for each person who kept some, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project kept any.

project_decisions.description: The facts a person in the project decided (ProjectFact), the last decision on each subject, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project decided any. A drafter treats each as supplied.

project_repository.description: The repository a researcher in the project chose last, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project has chosen one.

project_drafts.description: The latest version of each document drafted in the conversation's project, without its text, in the order first drafted, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds no drafted document.

project_intake.description: The researcher's current answers to the intake's setup questions beside the entry question, in the order they are asked, only for a question asked from the project's entry point, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or no such question has been answered. The entry question's answer is `project_entry`.
